doc: Every tool an agent may be granted, the minimum trust level that can hold it, and how the harness establishes whether it is actually present. `probe` is run by `mix harness.inspect`; a tool whose probe fails is reported unavailable and any gate depending on it reports `unavailable`, never `passed`. Tools marked `present: false` are documented-but-not-wired: the harness names them so an agent knows they were considered, and refuses to pretend they ran. `present` is the expectation for this repository's standard environment, not a claim about the machine you are on — the machine is asked by `probe`, and `probe` is what a gate believes. `mix harness.inspect --tools` prints both and marks every disagreement with `!`.

rules: A tool not listed here may not be granted. Adding one is a change to this file with a reason.
A granted tool still obeys the agent's trust level: the effective permission is the stricter of the two.
Infrastructure-write tools (wrangler, aiven, github release) are never granted to a generic implementation role.
MCP servers are pinned by version or revision in committed configuration. No unpinned @latest.
A tool whose probe fails is unavailable. Work that needed it is partially verified, and the report says so.
